message.content: {"summary":"You identify the central safety and professional-responsibility issues, name relevant stakeholders, and make a clear recommendation against shipping. Your two external case studies add useful context. To strengthen the report, assess the specific defect risks, explain when shipping could become acceptable after remediation, and support claims with more complete evidence and references.","next_steps":["In “Discussion: To Ship or Not to Ship,” specify the defects and use evidence to estimate failure likelihood and severity separately; avoid relying on general claims about possible harm.","In “The Most Ethical Path” and “Recommendation,” set evidence-based release criteria: describe remediation, testing, acceptable residual risk, and how affected stakeholders should weigh the results. Clarify the limits of the causal claim in the NHS example.","Complete and standardise the references, substantiate commercial claims, and proofread for grammatical errors. Consider a table or other visual to summarise defect risks and release criteria."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your Introduction identifies several ethical issues, links them to engineering organisations, and names stakeholders, including Rachel, her company, the contract company, and the health department. This meets the highest rubric level; maintain this strength by connecting each stakeholder’s interests to the later analysis.","C2":"Your Discussion presents reasons for and against shipping and reaches a clear recommendation. To reach Very good, develop the arguments with evidence, assess likelihood and severity rather than asserting risk, and explain how different stakeholders should make decisions.","C3":"The report’s sequence from Discussion to Conclusion and Recommendation is easy to follow, and your conclusion reflects the safety concerns raised. To reach Very good, make the case more compelling by systematically comparing risk-control options and showing how that assessment supports your recommendation.","C4":"The Most Ethical Path uses relevant NHS and Volkswagen examples and an engineering code to support your discussion. To reach Very good, broaden and deepen the evidence, add quantitative or specific evidence about the server defects and their risks, and qualify claims where the cited source does not establish causation.","C5":"Your report includes an abstract, introduction, body, conclusion, recommendation, and references. To reach Good, proofread for grammatical errors, complete and consistently format references, and add limited visual elements—such as a table comparing risks or release criteria—to support the discussion."}}
